title: Finite connected components of geometric coverings over a normal base
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme] which is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Assume that every local ring of $X$ is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $q:Z\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism], with $Z$ not assumed quasi-compact. Suppose that $q$ has the following valuation lifting property. For every valuation ring $R$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, every morphism $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, and every $X$-morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ over the restriction of $b$, there is a unique $X$-morphism $\widetilde a:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Z$ whose restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is $a$. Then every connected component of $|Z|$ (a maximal nonempty connected subset) is open and closed in $|Z|$. With the induced open subscheme structure, each such component $C\subset Z$ has finite etale surjective structural morphism $q|_C:C\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Thus $Z$ is the disjoint union of these connected finite etale $X$-schemes. The scheme $Z$ is allowed to be empty, in which case the indexing set of components is empty; the indexing set need not be finite in general.

source.place: Definition 7.3.1(3), p. 66; proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, connected geometric coverings are finite etale. Normality supplies geometric unibranchness by literature/stacks-project/properties.tex Tag 0BQ3, lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch. The open-and-closed component decomposition is the first paragraph of that proof; surjectivity follows from the nonempty open and closed image of a finite etale component over connected X.
